results.title: Chris’s Path to COO at Datastory: Data Stories That Inspire | Datastory
results.content: It’s easy to scroll LinkedIn and see endless success stories. Nice to read, but let’s be honest… they don’t always teach us much. That’s why I decided to flip the script. Instead of success stories, I’m sharing my 10 biggest fails in data engineering. Painful to write, but valuable for you not to repeat same misstakes. A few that still make me cringe: ⚡ Changing the schema in the gold layer broke hundreds of dashboards ⚡ Loading 150 tables into the lake when the business only needed 3 ⚡ Building one-off gold tables for every request made the warehouse unmanageable ⚡ Trusting green pipeline logs while the data itself was wrong ⚡ Creating a massive pipeline so complex nobody else dared touch it ⚡ Skipping data quality checks backfired with broken reports Each fail was painful, but each [...] with broken reports Each fail was painful, but each one came with a lesson I’ll never forget. 👉 I’ve put them all together in a new article so you can learn from my scars, not repeat them: [...] "First you need to go through the dark age. That's just part of it." Christian Klug said this about dashboard chaos, referencing Age of Empires. But he could have been talking about every messy data transformation I've ever seen. We just released Episode 4 of Data Breakthroughs (Cooking Data). The problem: A creative studio went from 15 controlled dashboards to 300+ in six months. Nobody knew which numbers to trust. Teams paralyzed. Excel making a comeback. Classic self-service BI disaster. Here's what Christian taught me while we solved it live: Listen first, challenge later. When rebuilding trust, accept stakeholders' KPIs as-is. Don't start by telling them they're measuring wrong. Get the quick win, then use that trust capital to refine. There's an early game and a late game. You

Title: Q&A with Datastory's Design Lead Emmy: Turning Data into Impactful Stories - Datastory Blog - Datastory
Q&A with Datastory's Design Lead Emmy: Turning Data into Impactful Stories. Discover how Emmy, Design Lead at Datastory, uses data storytelling to drive impact. Learn about her journey, a recent project with Tax Justice Network, and tips for better data storytelling. At Datastory, our mission is to transform complex data into stories that inspire change. In this Q&A, we sit down with our Design Lead,Emmy Bäckström, to explore her journey, the creative process behind our platform, and how we're helping users to tell compelling data stories, no matter their design background. ## From Creativity to Purpose: Emmy's Journey to Datastory. **Q:** *Can you tell us a bit about your background and how you became a designer at Datastory?*. **Emmy:** From a young age, I dreamed of having a job where I could be creative while making the world a better place. It was during high school when I read Hans Rosling's autobiography that I truly understood the power of information design. What really drew me here was the mission of using data to tell the world's most important stories in a way that people understand. **Q:** *What excites you most about working at Datastory?*. **Emmy:** I love the mix of working directly with our partners to create compelling narratives for their data, and also contributing to our platform that allows anyone to tell stories with data. It enables users to create entire websites packed with data-driven content, giving life to important stories that can drive real change. **Q:** *Can you share a recent project that you're particularly proud of?*. **Emmy:** We are currently collaborating with the Tax Justice Network to communicate their data on global corporate tax abuse. One of the things that excites me most is how the Datastory platform's data management capabilities unlock new possibilities. Want to learn more about how Tax Justice Network used Datastory to build a data-driven website? **Emmy:** At Datastory, we want to radically simplify data storytelling. To do that, we need to offer a tool that handles a lot of the complex but important tasks (like chart design and page layout) for you. **Emmy:** When telling stories with data, it's important to understand your audience and tailor your story to their needs.

Title: Interactive reports by Datastory: transform data into dynamic stories - Datastory Blog - Datastory
Interactive reports by Datastory: transform data into dynamic stories. Transform static reports into engaging, interactive experiences with Datastory's interactive reports feature, making data accessible and impactful. At Datastory, we believe that data is a story waiting to be told. Our**Interactive Reports** turn complex datasets into engaging, dynamic narratives that enable your audience to explore and understand your findings in a whole new way. Whether you're a researcher, policymaker, or an NGO, our platform helps you present your data in a format that's visually compelling, easy to navigate, and impactful. An interactive report is more than a document, it's a digital experience. Unlike traditional PDFs, which present static information, interactive reports empower your audience to interact directly with the data. This approach makes your content more accessible and actionable, turning data into stories that resonate with decision-makers, researchers, and the public. ## Key Features of Datastory's Interactive Reports. * **Dynamic Data Visualizations**: From interactive charts and graphs to rich data-driven maps, our platform lets your audience interact directly with your data. You can adapt these templates to your project, ensuring that your data is presented in the most effective way. With Datastory, you can update your interactive reports with real-time data, ensuring your audience always has access to the most current insights. In collaboration with the**Swedish House of Finance**, Datastory created an interactive report that evaluates the effectiveness of carbon pricing policies in reducing emissions, featuring dynamic data visualizations and research-backed insights. It provides a visually engaging way to understand how carbon pricing impacts industries and the environment. * **Interactive Comparisons**: The report offers users the ability to explore industry-level data on fossil emissions, with intuitive charts that showcase the outcomes of different carbon pricing strategies. **Academics & Researchers**: Present your research in a dynamic format, allowing your audience to easily explore data, compare insights, and understand your findings more deeply. ## Why Interactive Reports Outperform Static PDFs. Interactive reports allow users to interact with data—filtering, comparing, and analyzing it in real time—unlike static PDFs, which lock data into a fixed format. While PDFs present a snapshot in time, interactive reports can be continuously updated with live data, ensuring your audience has the latest insights.
